diagnostic_evidence.quote: We leave it as an exercise for the reader to prove the following property.
Graph-tree-induced edge coefficients are invariant to the choice of terminals up to a common factor.
Let $G$ be a directed 2-sp-graph with vertices $l$ and $r$ treated as terminals, and $\tau$ be its spanning tree.
Let us denote $e_0$'s vertices by $l$ and $r$ and treat them as the terminals.

issues.failure_explanation: By Definition (yei), the vector of $(G,\tau)$-induced coefficients is defined relative to a chosen terminal pair, and in the proof the terminals are always taken to be the endpoints of the row's edge $e_0$. Thus the machinery establishes, for each edge $e_0 \in \tau$, only the single-row identity (eqY) for the vector $y^{(e_0)}$ defined relative to $e_0$'s endpoints; different rows of the eigenvector equation are proven with different vectors. Reducing the eigenvalue equation $Y_\tau y_\tau = \frac{1}{n} y_\tau$ (hence the claim that $1/n$ is an eigenvalue of every spanning-tree submatrix, on which the whole theorem rests) to these per-row identities requires that all the vectors $y^{(e_0)}$, $e_0 \in \tau$, be proportional. That is exactly Proposition prop:added-1, which the paper states with no proof ("exercise for the reader") and never invokes in the proof. Without this unestablished invariance premise, the per-row identities do not assemble into one eigenvector equation, so the proof of the theorem is incomplete as written.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Supply a proof of Proposition prop:added-1 (a re-rooting argument for the decomposition tree parallel to the given proof of Proposition prw, tracking the $\psi$-coefficients and orientation signs under a change of terminals), and add an explicit assembly step noting that the eigenvector equation is invariant under scaling, so the per-row identities for the pairwise-proportional vectors $y^{(e_0)}$ combine into $Y_\tau y_\tau = \frac{1}{n} y_\tau$.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the main theorem (the deviation lower bound $\arccos(1/\sqrt{n})$ for the star spaces of all 2-sp-graphs) is incomplete: the eigenvector/eigenvalue claim for the spanning-tree submatrices is established only modulo the unproven terminal-invariance of the induced coefficients. The corollary on the sharpness of the Hypothesis estimate, which is derived from the theorem, inherits the same gap.
issues.title: Main theorem's proof silently relies on the unproven terminal-invariance of the (G,tau)-induced coefficients
issues.why_classification: The missing ingredient is a contained but genuinely nontrivial lemma proof (analogous to the page-long proof of Proposition prw already in the paper) plus a one-line assembly argument; the theorem and corollary survive at full stated strength, so no global restructuring, weakening, or loss of scope is required, but the repair is more than a routine local fix.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: measuring the least deviation of the given subspace from all the same-dimensional coordinate subspaces
In all the experiments we have conducted for various $n$ and $k$, this value was equal to $\arccos(1 / \sqrt{n})$.

issues.failure_explanation: Distance(A) returns the least deviation of the subspace from the coordinate subspaces, i.e. an angle in $[0,\pi/2]$ whose extremal value is $\arccos(1/\sqrt{n})$ (as the surrounding text states). Both conditional tests in alg:cap2 compare this angle with the number $1/\sqrt{n}$ instead. Since $\arccos(x) > x$ for all $x \in (0,1)$, every near-extremal subspace satisfies $d > 1/\sqrt{n} + \varepsilon$, so the algorithm as written would print "The hypothesis is solved in negative" and return $-1$ precisely on its own extremal subspaces, and the collection test $d > 1/\sqrt{n} - \varepsilon$ would admit subspaces far from extremal. The thresholds must be $\arccos(1/\sqrt{n}) \pm \varepsilon$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace both occurrences of the threshold $1/sqrt(n)$ in the two conditional tests of alg:cap2 by $\arccos(1/\sqrt{n})$.
issues.overall_effect: The appendix algorithm's stated input-output contract (detect a negative resolution of the Hypothesis; accumulate exactly the near-extremal subspaces) fails as written; no theorem, proposition, or other formal claim depends on this pseudocode.
issues.title: Extremal-subspace algorithm compares the angle-valued distance against the cosine threshold 1/sqrt(n)
issues.why_classification: A single forced local correction, uniquely determined by the surrounding text (which fixes the extremal target value at $\arccos(1/\sqrt{n})$), restores the algorithm's stated behavior, and no formal result, guarantee, or advertised scope is affected.
